compose._doc_post_hook: init-mirrors.sh converges the admin user, the mirror owner, mirror_policy.exclude (by DELETION) and every derived mirror. Its header claimed 'container-init calls this' but nothing did — no systemd unit, cron entry, compose hook or ship step referenced it, the deploy only COPIED it to configs/, and a stale April copy sat at the deploy root. So the mirror set only ever moved when somebody ran it by hand (17 -> 32 on 2026-09-05) and drifted the rest of the time. Declaring it here runs it on every ship under the engine's revision-scoped receipt (<DEPLOY_PATH>/.posthook-receipt), which is wiped first and written only on exit 0 — a hook that did not run can no longer report green.

gitea._mirrors_doc: Mirrors are DERIVED, not listed here. The consolidator expands mirror_policy against the fetched GitHub inventory (9_others/src/inputs/github-repos.json) into the concrete gitea.mirrors map, setting private:true from each repo's real visibility. Hand-listing them drifted: `front` pointed at a repo that has never existed and silently never synced, and `cloud-data` — private on GitHub — was mirrored WITHOUT private:true, i.e. published.

mirror_policy._include_forks_doc: FairEmail and octocode are upstream forks; mirroring them copies other people's code with no backup value. Flip to true to include them.
mirror_policy._exclude_doc: Repo names to skip entirely (exact match against github-repos.json .repos[].name — see expandGiteaMirrors in 1_cloud-configs/src/derive/cloud-data-config-consolidated.ts). Empty = mirror every non-fork repo in the inventory. cloud-vault is hard-excluded as defense in depth: mirror privacy otherwise depends solely on the inventory's private:true flag, and that same derived-flag mechanism already republished cloud-data (also private) as a public mirror once before it existed (see _mirrors_doc above). A credential store must not depend on a single flag being right every time.
